parameters.Temperature_Source_Reference: Specific values for High/Low Temperature should be determined referencing MIL-HDBK-310 and Method 501.7, as MIL-STD-810H Method 503.7 does not directly specify these values for Procedure I-A.
parameters.Transfer_Time_Basis: MIL-STD-810H Method 503.7 implies rapid transfer for 'Temperature Shock' but does not specify a concrete maximum transfer time. '≤ 1 minute' is a common practical target derived from general test practices for shock simulation.
parameters.Procedure_Selection_Considerations_EN: Prior to test, explicitly consider 'anticipated operational exposure temperatures' and 'logistical or deployment configuration of the material' as per MIL-STD-810H paragraph 2.2.1. These factors are crucial for test design and logic.
parameters.Procedure_Selection_Considerations_ZH: 測試前，需根據 MIL-STD-810H 2.2.1 節，明確考量「預期服役的暴露溫度」及「物料的後勤或部署配置」。這些因素對於測試設計與邏輯至關重要。

parameters.Shock_Direction_Requirement_ZH: MIL-STD-810H Method 503.7 程序 I-A 要求對每個適當條件執行至少一次衝擊，例如：低溫至高溫，以及高溫至低溫 (如適用)。此 JSON 描述的是單次衝擊事件的參數，可能需要重複以涵蓋反向衝擊。
parameters.Rate_of_Temperature_Change: As rapid as practicable, consistent with test chamber capabilities and item characteristics, to simulate shock conditions. Specific target rate should be defined in the test plan.
parameters.Stabilization_Criteria: Thermal stabilization is achieved when the item temperature is changing at a rate no greater than 2°C (3.6°F) per hour for three consecutive readings, or as otherwise specified in the detailed test plan.
parameters.Number_of_Shocks_per_Direction: At least one shock cycle per required direction (e.g., one Low-to-High, one High-to-Low).

tests.Condition: Stabilize item at T-initial (e.g., Low Temperature or High Temperature) according to the defined stabilization criteria before initiating the transfer.

Hold item at T-final until thermally stabilized according to the defined stabilization criteria.

Upon completion of all required cycles/shocks, remove the item from the chamber. Perform required functional tests and thorough visual examination for any physical damage, deformation, or performance degradation. Document all observations and test results.

parameters.Profile: Tailored to specific operational environment and threat scenario per MIL-STD-810H Method 522.2 Procedure I guidelines, focusing on empirical determination of actual ballistic shock levels.
parameters.Test_Article_Mounting: Installed in Ballistic Hull & Turret (BH&T) that replicates the full-size vehicle, ensuring representative shock transmission.

parameters.Tailoring_Details: The specific threat scenario, number of shots, measurement techniques, and data analysis plan are determined through the tailoring process based on the item's lifecycle environmental profile and mission requirements.
parameters.Rate_of_Change: Not a direct input parameter for the shock event itself, but critical for analysis of shock pulse characteristics (e.g., rise/fall times, peak rates) derived from the acquired data.
parameters.Humidity: Ambient relative humidity during the test will be recorded. While not a primary parameter for ballistic shock generation, it contributes to the overall environmental test conditions.
parameters.Temperature: Ambient temperature during the test will be recorded. Similar to humidity, it provides context for environmental conditions during the test.
parameters.Duration: Overall test campaign duration will depend on setup, firing schedule, and data analysis requirements. The duration of an individual shock event is typically in milliseconds.

tests.Condition: Perform a thorough visual inspection, photographic documentation, and functional check of the test article to establish a baseline condition as per the test plan. Record any pre-existing anomalies.
Stabilize the test article to ambient laboratory conditions (or specified pre-test operating conditions) for a minimum of 4 hours prior to mounting or as defined by the test plan.

Install the test article in the BH&T facility, ensuring proper mounting and securing as per design specifications. Attach all required accelerometers and high-speed data acquisition equipment to capture shock response at designated points. Verify all instrumentation is operational and calibrated.

Conduct live fire testing by firing specific threat rounds at defined distances and orientations as per the tailored test plan. Acquire high-speed shock time-history data for each individual event. Ensure safety protocols are strictly followed.
Immediately after each shot or sequence of shots, verify the integrity, quality, and completeness of the acquired shock data. Perform quick-look analysis to ensure data capture was successful.

After all shock exposures are completed, perform a comprehensive visual inspection, photographic documentation, and functional check of the test article as per the test plan. Document any observed anomalies, damage, or failures induced by the test.

Analyze the acquired shock time-history data to determine actual shock levels (e.g., peak acceleration, SRS). Compare these empirically determined levels against specified default shock levels and acceptance criteria. Generate a comprehensive test report detailing procedures, results, analysis, and conclusions.

tests.Condition: Install dummy test item to determine and confirm appropriate explosive 'recipe' (e.g., explosive weight, standoff, hydraulic displacement) to achieve shock levels defined in Table 522.2-I and Figure 522.2-1, before installing the operational test item.
Mount test item using the same hardware as in actual armored vehicles, orienting it to produce maximum shock in the 'worst-case' axis. Expose item to LSBSS generated ballistic shock.

parameters.Level Determination Method: Calculate Shock Response Spectrum (SRS) and select an enveloping half-sine acceleration pulse
parameters.Level Determination Caveat: Method may result in overtest at low frequencies
parameters.Inherent Test Characteristics: Drop table test generates a half-sine acceleration pulse, which differs significantly from actual ballistic shock. It may overtest at low frequencies and undertest at high frequencies, but is generally acceptable.

tests.Condition: Perform operational check and record data for later comparison.
Simulate ballistic shock via high-frequency drop table
Perform operational check and compare with pre-test data.

parameters.Description_EN: Physical damage from moisture freezing and thawing in crevices
parameters.Description_ZH: 模擬水分滲入縫隙後結冰膨脹再融化產生的物理結構破壞
parameters.Moisture Element: Sufficient water introduced via water vapor, steam, vapor generator, or other means to penetrate crevices.
parameters.Rate of Temperature Change: Not exceeding 3°C (5°F) per minute (each phase transition within 3 hours)
parameters.Stabilization Holding Time: 1 hour (after temperature stabilization for each phase)

tests.Condition: Visually inspect and document initial condition of the test item.
Introduce sufficient moisture to achieve or near saturation, considering dewpoint and precipitation requirements, prior to the first cold phase.

Perform 20 cycles of freezing and thawing. Each cycle includes holding at -10°C (14°F) for 1 hour after stabilization, followed by a transition to 4°C (39°F), holding for 1 hour after stabilization, then transitioning back. Temperature change rate between phases shall not exceed 3°C (5°F) per minute, with each transition phase completed within 3 hours.
Inspect for cracked seals, housing separation, component distortion, and other physical damage; document findings.

parameters.Condition: Rapid temperature drop below dew point
parameters.Description_EN: Simulation of moisture condensation (fogging) on/in materiel
parameters.Description_ZH: 起霧測試，模擬由濕度與溫度變化造成的裝備內部或光學表面起霧
parameters.InitialColdChamberTemperature_Note: 10°C (18°F) below freezing point, or as specified by requirements
parameters.CycleSteps_EN: Steps 'Cold Soak', 'Transfer to Warm Chamber', and 'Condensation & Operational Test' constitute one cycle and are repeated for the specified number of cycles.
parameters.TransferRequirement_EN: Transfer test item as quickly as possible between chambers
parameters.TransferRecommendation_EN: Use an insulated transport container for transfer
parameters.PostTestExamination_EN: Perform a complete visual and operational examination and record results upon completion of all cycles

tests.Description_EN: Adjust chamber temperature to specified initial cold temperature and maintain until test item temperature stabilizes, then for an additional hour. This is the first step of each test cycle.
Rapidly transfer the test item from the cold chamber to the warm chamber. An insulated transport container is recommended. This is the second step of each test cycle.

Subject item to conditions inducing internal/external fogging. Raise temperature at a rate not exceeding specified maximum, while maintaining specified relative humidity. Initiate operational and performance tests within the specified time window after transfer completion. This is the third step of each test cycle.
Upon completion of all test cycles, perform a complete visual and operational examination and record results. Refer to MIL-STD-810H paragraph 4.3.2 for failure handling guidance.

parameters.Description_EN: Single Exciter Single Axis (SESA) Time Waveform Replication: Replicate real field-measured time waveforms on a vibration table, adhering to MIL-STD-810H Method 525.2.
parameters.Description_ZH: 單軸/單激振器 (SESA) 時域波形重現：將實地錄製的複雜時域波形直接在振動台上重播，符合 MIL-STD-810H Method 525.2 規範。
parameters.Exciter Configuration: Single Exciter Single Axis (SESA) Time Waveform Replication (MIL-STD-810H Method 525.2 Section 1.2.2)
parameters.Calibration Requirements: System exciters, all transducers, signal conditioning equipment, independent measurement systems, and exciter control system hardware must be calibrated according to MIL-STD-810H Method 525.2 Section 4.2.1.
parameters.Data Retention Requirements: ASCII format reference, control, and drive time waveform files must be accessible at all times for independent verification of time waveform replication adequacy (MIL-STD-810H Method 525.2 Section 4.2.1).
parameters.Tolerance Definition: Test tolerance criteria must be established prior to testing, considering guidance from MIL-STD-810H Method 525.2 Section 1.2.1 and applied as per Section 4.2.2.
parameters.Instrumentation Requirements: Instrumentation must meet the requirements specified in MIL-STD-810H Method 525.2 Section 4.4, including but not limited to sensors, data acquisition systems, and shakers.
parameters.Information Requirements: All information required by MIL-STD-810H Method 525.2 Section 3 (pre-test, during-test, post-test) must be documented and available.
parameters.Test Facility Requirements: Test facility must comply with MIL-STD-810H Method 525.2 Section 4.1.
parameters.Test Interruption Handling: Procedures for handling test interruptions must follow MIL-STD-810H Method 525.2 Section 4.3.
parameters.Test Execution Procedures: Test execution, including preparation and pre-test checks, must adhere to MIL-STD-810H Method 525.2 Section 4.5.

tests.Condition: Perform initial calibration of all exciters, transducers, and control systems as per MIL-STD-810H Method 525.2 Section 4.2.1.
Determine system transfer function using low-level random excitation.
Iteratively correct drive signal to match target field waveform within established tolerance criteria as per MIL-STD-810H Method 525.2 Section 4.2.2.
Conduct post-test examination, data archiving, and final reporting as per MIL-STD-810H Method 525.2 Section 3.

parameters.Description_EN: Procedure II - Internally Excited Vibration
parameters.Description_ZH: 程序 II - 內部激發震動 (Type II)
parameters.Profile: Refer to MIL-STD-810H for specific sub-procedure requirements
parameters.Temperature: Not Specified in Reference Document (MIL-STD-810H Method 528.1 does not specify explicit temperature values for internally excited vibration Type II beyond typical operating ambient)
parameters.Humidity: Not Specified in Reference Document (MIL-STD-810H Method 528.1 does not specify explicit humidity values for internally excited vibration Type II)
parameters.Pressure: Not Specified in Reference Document (MIL-STD-810H Method 528.1 does not specify explicit pressure values for internally excited vibration Type II)
parameters.Duration: Not Specified in Reference Document (Duration is typically tied to functional operation cycles or specific operational scenarios for internally excited vibration Type II)
parameters.RateOfChange: Not Applicable for Internally Excited Vibration Type II (Rate of Change typically applies to environmental parameters like temperature or pressure changes)
parameters.PurposeAndScope: The primary purpose of Type II vibration testing is from the perspective of mechanical suitability, not structural propagation noise. For noise suitability, refer to MIL-STD-740-2.
parameters.AcceptanceCriteriaGuidance: Must carefully determine all functions the equipment must maintain under normal shipboard vibration. Functional requirements, including appropriate test acceptance standards, must be met and verified during vibration testing (Refer MIL-STD-810H Section 2.4 Guidance for Specifiers).

tests.Condition: Perform necessary pre-test setup, equipment calibration, and verification of initial functional requirements as per MIL-STD-810H guidance (e.g., Section 2.4). Specifically, ensure compliance with Section 5.2.2 balancing procedures for unbalanced rotating components found in shipboard equipment prior to vibration exposure.

Execute Procedure II - Internally Excited Vibration per MIL-STD-810H. For internally excited vibrations from unbalanced rotating components, specifically incorporate and execute Section 5.2.2 balancing procedures. Monitor functional performance and integrity throughout the exposure period.

Perform post-test examination, comprehensive functional checks, and verify equipment against defined acceptance criteria (as determined by 'Guidance for Specifiers' in MIL-STD-810H 2.4). Document any observed degradation, damage, or functional failures.
